analysis:
This batch changes only the CI threat-review tooling and its documentation. It touches no provider, coordinator wire, attestation, crypto or inference code, so none of the provider assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011) are directly affected.

Workflow (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml):
- The maintainer workflow_dispatch review path is removed. This drops the pr_number input, the inline Python resolver (base 90-115) and the dispatch branch of BEDROCK_SCAN_ENABLED (base 68). The review job now runs only on pull_request_target (head 67-69), which narrows the paid trigger surface.
- Preflight now defaults to true (head 12). The preflight job itself is unchanged and checks out the maintainer-selected revision.
- THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA now comes only from event data (head 128).
- The scanner is still checked out from the default branch with persist-credentials false (head 76-83), so PR code is not executed.
- Fork PRs still get Bedrock only when the BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS variable is set (head 64).
- Limits are raised: timeout 20 to 60 minutes (head 55), a 3000s scan deadline (head 131), and workload call policy defaults of 500 calls and 16384 output tokens (head 135-137). These are cost and availability knobs that maintainers can lower through Actions variables. Concurrency cancel-in-progress per PR (head 73) limits stacking from repeated synchronize events.
- The 3000s deadline fits within the 3600s role duration (head 116).

Diagnostics (.github/scripts/threat_review/diagnostics.py, head 80-83): the artifact adds finished plus bedrock_call_* counters. These are non-content values from the snapshot. SHA validation (head 86-88) and suppression of exception text remain.

Documentation (build.md head 258-267 and the changelog) describes these changes. The changelog's claims that job reruns are disabled and that incomplete reviews cannot grant clearance rely on enforcement in scanner and gate scripts that were not supplied. The visible workflow only adds advisory summary text (head 177).

Integration should check:
- that threat-review-gate.py and the state/budget code enforce the claimed rerun denial and workload ceiling;
- that 'finished' and the counters cannot carry arbitrary text.

No provider-threat-model regression was identified.
